subject: Renewal pricing options and short-term surge protection
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@aperturelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com
Date: 2027-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — need options for next term

Hi Vanessa,

Quick note as we start planning our renewal: our usage forecasts show a 2.5x increase next 12 months driven by a product launch in Q4. Current commit will not cover that. Can you send options that balance unit price stability and capacity — we care about latency SLOs, and would prefer something that avoids surprise overage billing.

Specific asks:
- A short-term path (3–6 months) to bridge until we finalize a larger commit
- A multi-quarter price-hold or anchor credit we can rely on
- Any upfront credits or onboarding concessions for a larger multi-year commit

Procurement looped in (procurement@aperturelabs.com) for PO timing. Would appreciate a concise set of alternatives we can circulate internally.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Head of Platform, Aperture Labs
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@aperturelabs.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — need options for next term

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a one-page proposal and a draft SOW with three pragmatic paths based on typical customers in your usage band. High level:

Option A — 12-month renewal (recommended if you want predictable ops):
- 15% renewal discount on list unit rates
- One-time anchor credit equal to 20% of your prior 12-month spend, applied as a billing credit at signing if you commit to >=3x baseline capacity for 12 months
- Standard SLAs; no price increases during term

Option B — 24-month price-hold (best for long-term predictability):
- 10% discount, 24-month price-hold on serving rates
- Smaller onboarding credit (10% of prior spend)
- Requires minimal 2x baseline committed capacity

Option C — Short bridge + surge insurance (fastest to execute):
- 6-month term with a price-hold at current rates; optional burst insurance (separate monthly fee) that guarantees access to a shared burst pool at capped rates
- We can include a one-time onboarding credit (negotiable) if you execute the amendment this week

Attachments: Aperture_Renewal_Options_v1.pdf, SOW_draft.docx (proposal + draft term language).

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick internal sync between our SE and your platform leads to size burst needs, 2) if Option C looks right we can run a 6-month amendment and include a PO path for procurement. Ben — can you confirm burst sizing note below?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@aperturelabs.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com
Date: 2027-07-30T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — need options for next term

Thanks Vanessa. Jordan — quick technical context on the burst insurance and capacity options so you can align with engineering:

- Burst pool: shared pooled GPUs with capped per-token rates for steady-state and higher caps for sustained bursts. Good fit for unpredictable spikes while keeping base commit modest.
- Dedicated + autoscale: if you expect sustained 2.5x utilization, Dedicated capacity with autoscale and a small reserved commit gives lower per-token costs and consistent latency.
- Workload optimizations: spot-checking your sample calls, we can likely reduce 12–18% token cost with quantization + model selection without affecting quality for most queries. That reduces the effective price you pay and can change the recommended commit tier.

I can run a short demo next Tue (Aug 3) that shows burst behavior and the cost delta between shared burst vs. dedicated config.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@aperturelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-31T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — need options for next term

Vanessa / Ben — thanks, that helped. Internally we've talked through the options and procurement prefers a short path to avoid committing to a full-year until after launch. Aperture would like to proceed with Option C (6-month bridge + surge insurance) with two asks:
1) A one-time onboarding credit of $15k to offset implementation work
2) Confirmation the burst insurance cap (per-token rate) will be fixed for the 6-month term

If those are acceptable we'll route a PO. Procurement, can you confirm target PO date?

Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: procurement@aperturelabs.com, Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@aperturelabs.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — need options for next term

Hi Jordan — Marissa from Redwood Finance. We can approve a one-time onboarding credit of $15,000 on the condition that: 1) the 6-month amendment is signed, 2) Aperture accepts the attached amendment template (we'll finalize with any legal redlines), and 3) payment terms are standard net30 after the amendment effective date.

Attachment: Amendment_template.docx — it includes the burst insurance rate table (fixed for the 6-month window) and billing milestone schedule (50% on effective date, 50% at month 3). If procurement can confirm the PO by Friday (Aug 6) we'll queue DocuSign and reserve the burst capacity for launch week.

Thanks — Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jmeyers@aperturelabs.com>, procurement@aperturelabs.com

- Redwood will provision Option C (6-month price-hold + burst insurance) and apply a $15k onboarding credit after amendment is signed.

- Ben will run the demo Aug 3 to validate burst sizing; Marissa will finalize billing milestones once the amendment is signed.

Procurement — please reply with the PO number or timing and we'll route the DocuSign for signature.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
